mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate directly reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing the present value of future cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in low-rate periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 7.5%, it signals a weak labor market that typically precedes corporate earnings deterioration and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The unemployment rate exceeding 7.5% fails to produce negative 5-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and business investment, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-rate regime (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%), a further decline in the federal funds rate signals an aggressive monetary easing policy that boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS < 0.5%, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output and strong corporate sector activity, which consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The INDPRO trend fails to predict positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances, or the Rank IC is below 0.02 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) exceed 850,000 units, it signals a strong housing market that typically precedes increased consumer spending and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 850.0 fails to produce positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over a 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint movement (PAYEMS up and UNRATE down) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in more than 40% of instances, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of real GDP (GDPC1 > 15500 billion) indicates sustained economic expansion, which supports positive equity returns, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When GDPC1 > 15500 billion, the 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a 2-year rolling window.
